easy.question: Who called them at the beginning of the passage?
answers: Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
Joshua called Korah and his brothers
Moses called the leaders of the people
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says Joshua called the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh — so Joshua summoned them.

easy.question: What did Joshua praise the tribes of Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh for?
answers: For building an altar on the west bank
For keeping Moses' command and obeying him
For bringing many offerings to Joshua
easy.explanation: Verses 2–3 state they kept all that Moses commanded and kept their brethren — meaning they obeyed Moses' commands.

easy.question: What did Joshua do at the end of the passage for those he called?
answers: He judged them and imposed a punishment
He declared war against them
He blessed them and sent them to their tents
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says 'So Joshua blessed them and sent them away' — he blessed them and dismissed them to their tents.

medium.question: Why does Joshua say, 'Now the LORD your God hath given rest unto your brethren,' and ask them to return to their possessions?
answers: Because the temporary settlement had no housing
Because their brethren in the west had subdued the enemies and possession was secured, so they could return to their holdings across the Jordan
Because Moses commanded them to leave the area
medium.explanation: The meaning is that the Canaanite wars were finished (the people were subdued) and the LORD gave rest, so they could return to the inheritance given them beyond the Jordan.

medium.question: In the phrase 'kept the charge of the commandment', what does 'charge' mean?
answers: Duty to observe and obey the command — keeping the commandments
A sacred object in the tabernacle
A military guard protecting the land
medium.explanation: Here 'charge' refers to duty and faithful observance of the commandments given by Moses/God.

medium.question: Which central instruction does Joshua repeat in verse 5?
answers: To guard only the borders of the city
To love the LORD, walk in all His ways, keep His commandments and serve Him with all your heart and soul
To pay tribute to the leaders
medium.explanation: Verse 5 commands them to love the LORD, walk in His ways and keep His commandments — a central call to faithful obedience.

challenge.question: To whom does the phrase 'the half-tribe of Manasseh' in verse 1 refer?
answers: The portion of the tribe of Manasseh that received an inheritance beyond the Jordan (east of the Jordan)
The portion of Manasseh living in the Samaria kingdom
Half of the people who remained in the wilderness and did not enter the land
challenge.explanation: The text specifies 'on the other side of Jordan', referring to the half of Manasseh that received territory east of the Jordan.

challenge.question: The phrase 'on the other side of Jordan' in the passage indicates that...
answers: Their possessions were west of the Jordan
Their possessions were east of the Jordan River
They lived only by the Sea of Galilee
challenge.explanation: 'On the other side of Jordan' means across the Jordan — i.e., to the east of the river.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'be very diligent to do' (kept back in the Hebrew) indicate about Joshua's tone of warning?
answers: He gave a general instruction and was not worried about disobedience
He warned sternly and urged strict faithfulness to the commandments
He treated the matter lightly and as unimportant
challenge.explanation: The addition 'very' with the command implies urgency and stern admonition to be scrupulously faithful to the commands.

questions.question: To whom does the phrase 'the half-tribe of Manasseh' in verse 1 refer?
answers: The portion of the tribe of Manasseh that received an inheritance beyond the Jordan (east of the Jordan)
The portion of Manasseh living in the Samaria kingdom
Half of the people who remained in the wilderness and did not enter the land
questions.explanation: The text specifies 'on the other side of Jordan', referring to the half of Manasseh that received territory east of the Jordan.

questions.question: The phrase 'on the other side of Jordan' in the passage indicates that...
answers: Their possessions were west of the Jordan
Their possessions were east of the Jordan River
They lived only by the Sea of Galilee
questions.explanation: 'On the other side of Jordan' means across the Jordan — i.e., to the east of the river.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'be very diligent to do' (kept back in the Hebrew) indicate about Joshua's tone of warning?
answers: He gave a general instruction and was not worried about disobedience
He warned sternly and urged strict faithfulness to the commandments
He treated the matter lightly and as unimportant
questions.explanation: The addition 'very' with the command implies urgency and stern admonition to be scrupulously faithful to the commands.

easy.question: Who gave the half-tribe of Manasseh their portion in Bashan?
answers: Moses
Joshua
Aaron
easy.explanation: Verse 7 notes that Moses gave half the tribe of Manasseh their possession in Bashan — Moses is credited with that grant.

easy.question: What did Joshua do after their portion was given?
answers: He rebuked them
He sent them to their tents and blessed them
He left them at Shiloh
easy.explanation: The verse states he sent them to their tents and blessed them.

easy.question: Where did the Reubenites, Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh go according to the verse?
answers: To Jerusalem
Only to the land of Canaan
To the land of Gilead — their possession
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says they went to the land of Gilead, to their possession — their allotted territory.

medium.question: Where did Joshua give the other half of Manasseh's portion according to the verse?
answers: In Bashan
Only in the land of Canaan
With their brethren on this side of the Jordan (westward)
medium.explanation: Verse 7 explains half was given by Moses in Bashan and the other half Joshua gave among their brethren on this side of the Jordan — i.e., westward.

medium.question: What does the word 'possessions' mean in the phrase 'return with much possessions to your tents'?
answers: Wealth and property (goods, money)
Livestock only
Losses and damages
medium.explanation: Here 'possessions' refers to wealth and goods — silver, gold and booty mentioned in the verse.

medium.question: Why did the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh go to Gilead according to the verse?
answers: Because they wanted to leave their goods at Shiloh
Because it was their inheritance given by the LORD through Moses
Because Joshua drove them out
medium.explanation: The verse explains they went to the land of Gilead, of their possession, as given by the LORD through Moses.

challenge.question: What is implied by the command 'divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren'?
answers: That they should not take any spoil at all
That the spoil should be shared with their brethren as a practice of sharing victory
That the spoil should be sold to foreigners
challenge.explanation: The verse calls for sharing the spoil with their brethren — requiring distribution rather than keeping it all.

challenge.question: From where did the Reubenites, Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh depart according to the verse?
answers: Hebron
Jericho
Shiloh
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 says they departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go to Gilead.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses' mean in this context?
answers: That the inheritance was given by the LORD and executed by Moses
That Moses took the land in his own name without divine command
That the land was taken by Moses' force without relation to God
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates the allocation was by the LORD's command and implemented through Moses — it was God's decision carried out by Moses.

questions.question: What is implied by the command 'divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren'?
answers: That they should not take any spoil at all
That the spoil should be shared with their brethren as a practice of sharing victory
That the spoil should be sold to foreigners
questions.explanation: The verse calls for sharing the spoil with their brethren — requiring distribution rather than keeping it all.

questions.question: From where did the Reubenites, Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh depart according to the verse?
answers: Hebron
Jericho
Shiloh
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says they departed from Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go to Gilead.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'according to the word of the LORD by the hand of Moses' mean in this context?
answers: That the inheritance was given by the LORD and executed by Moses
That Moses took the land in his own name without divine command
That the land was taken by Moses' force without relation to God
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates the allocation was by the LORD's command and implemented through Moses — it was God's decision carried out by Moses.

paragraphs.title: A Large Altar Built by the Jordan

easy.question: Who built the altar according to the verse?
answers: The children of Reuben, the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
All the tribes of Israel together
Only the Levites
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly names the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh as the builders of the altar.

easy.question: What did these tribes build by the Jordan?
answers: A fortress
A temple
A large altar
easy.explanation: The verse speaks of 'a great altar to see to' — they built a large visible altar by the Jordan.

easy.question: Where was the altar built according to the verse?
answers: In the northern hills
By the borderlands of the Jordan
On the shore of the Dead Sea
easy.explanation: The text says they came to the borderlands of the Jordan and built the altar there — the Jordan borderlands.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'a great altar to see to' mean in this context?
answers: An altar built to be conspicuous and visible to all
A small private altar for internal use
An altar solely for burial purposes
medium.explanation: 'To see to' indicates it was meant to be seen — a conspicuous public altar visible to others.

medium.question: In the phrase 'unto the other side of Jordan', what does 'other side' indicate?
answers: The eastern side (east of the Jordan River)
The western side (west of the Jordan)
The shores of the Sea of Galilee only
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the side opposite the main part of Israel — across the Jordan, i.e., the east bank.

medium.question: What reaction is most likely to have arisen among the Israelites when they heard that this altar was built?
answers: That communal tradition was kept without concern
That it signaled an intention to share worship among all tribes
Fear that the altar signified a rebellious or divided approach to worship
medium.explanation: Building altars outside the central sanctuary often raised fear of split worship or idolatry, so a reaction of alarm is likely.

challenge.question: Why does the verse describe the place as 'over against the land of Canaan' — what's the geographical meaning?
answers: The altar was established on the east side of the Jordan, opposite Canaan on the west
The altar was set deep inside Canaan among the southern tribes
The altar was on the Mediterranean coast
challenge.explanation: 'Over against the land of Canaan' indicates the altar stood on the side opposite Canaan — east of the Jordan facing Canaan.

challenge.question: What are the possible religious-social implications of certain tribes building 'a great altar' at that site?
answers: It has no religious effect; it's only a territorial marker
It could be seen as establishing a separate cultic center and lead to disputes over sacrificial rights
It shows social hierarchy based solely on wealth
challenge.explanation: An altar of that size outside the central sanctuary could be perceived as an attempt to create an independent ritual center, risking division over worship.

challenge.question: Which tactical detail in these verses helps explain the tension between the tribes?
answers: The altar was erected only at night
The altar was built by the Jordan — on the eastern bank facing Canaan — making it visible to the rest of Israel
The altar was made entirely of pure gold
challenge.explanation: The key detail is that the altar was on the Jordan facing Canaan, making it plainly visible to other Israelites and heightening concerns about a separate cult.

questions.question: Why does the verse describe the place as 'over against the land of Canaan' — what's the geographical meaning?
answers: The altar was established on the east side of the Jordan, opposite Canaan on the west
The altar was set deep inside Canaan among the southern tribes
The altar was on the Mediterranean coast
questions.explanation: 'Over against the land of Canaan' indicates the altar stood on the side opposite Canaan — east of the Jordan facing Canaan.

questions.question: What are the possible religious-social implications of certain tribes building 'a great altar' at that site?
answers: It has no religious effect; it's only a territorial marker
It could be seen as establishing a separate cultic center and lead to disputes over sacrificial rights
It shows social hierarchy based solely on wealth
questions.explanation: An altar of that size outside the central sanctuary could be perceived as an attempt to create an independent ritual center, risking division over worship.

questions.question: Which tactical detail in these verses helps explain the tension between the tribes?
answers: The altar was erected only at night
The altar was built by the Jordan — on the eastern bank facing Canaan — making it visible to the rest of Israel
The altar was made entirely of pure gold
questions.explanation: The key detail is that the altar was on the Jordan facing Canaan, making it plainly visible to other Israelites and heightening concerns about a separate cult.

paragraphs.title: Assembly and the Sending of Phinehas

easy.question: Where did the whole congregation of Israel assemble according to verse 12?
answers: Shiloh
Jerusalem
The hill country of Ephraim
easy.explanation: Verse 12 says they assembled at Shiloh — the place of the assembly.

easy.question: Who was sent to the Reubenites, Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh according to verse 13?
answers: Joshua son of Nun
Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest
Caleb
easy.explanation: Verse 13 identifies Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest as the one sent to them.

easy.question: How many princes accompanied Phinehas according to verse 14?
answers: Two
Five
Ten
easy.explanation: The verse states 'ten princes' — ten leading men accompanied him.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the assembly at Shiloh as described in verse 12?
answers: To celebrate a festival
To go up in arms against them (to make war)
To build a new altar
medium.explanation: Verse 12 indicates the congregation gathered 'to go up to war against them' — an assembly for military action was intended.

medium.question: In the phrase 'ten princes, of each chief house a prince', what does 'prince' mean?
answers: A leader or head of a family/household
A Levitical priest
A senior warrior
medium.explanation: Here 'prince' denotes a leader or representative — a head of a father's household.

medium.question: Whom did those ten princes represent according to verse 14?
answers: Each tribe separately
A father's household (heads of families)
Priests only
medium.explanation: The verse says 'a prince for every chief house' — each prince represented a household or family unit.

challenge.question: What does the sending to the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh tell us about their geographic location?
answers: That they were settled in the land of Gilead east of the Jordan
That they lived in Shiloh near the tabernacle
That they had fled to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The text refers to the land of Gilead, indicating they settled east of the Jordan in Gilead.

challenge.question: What is the most likely meaning of the phrase 'to go up against them' in this context?
answers: To go to see them only
To go on a pilgrimage to them
To attack them / go to war against them
challenge.explanation: The context is a gathered congregation 'to go up to war' — so 'to go up against them' means launching an attack.

challenge.question: Why was sending Phinehas the priest significant socially and religiously?
answers: Because he was a military commander and it signaled a purely military action
Because as a priest his involvement showed the matter had religious as well as civil importance
Because he was a foreigner unrelated to Israel
challenge.explanation: Phinehas' role as priest indicates the issue touched on religious authority and discipline, not only military concerns.

questions.question: What does the sending to the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh tell us about their geographic location?
answers: That they were settled in the land of Gilead east of the Jordan
That they lived in Shiloh near the tabernacle
That they had fled to Egypt
questions.explanation: The text refers to the land of Gilead, indicating they settled east of the Jordan in Gilead.

questions.question: What is the most likely meaning of the phrase 'to go up against them' in this context?
answers: To go to see them only
To go on a pilgrimage to them
To attack them / go to war against them
questions.explanation: The context is a gathered congregation 'to go up to war' — so 'to go up against them' means launching an attack.

questions.question: Why was sending Phinehas the priest significant socially and religiously?
answers: Because he was a military commander and it signaled a purely military action
Because as a priest his involvement showed the matter had religious as well as civil importance
Because he was a foreigner unrelated to Israel
questions.explanation: Phinehas' role as priest indicates the issue touched on religious authority and discipline, not only military concerns.

easy.question: Who is speaking in verse 16?
answers: The whole congregation of the LORD
Joshua alone
The tribes beyond the Jordan
easy.explanation: Verse 16 begins 'Thus saith the whole congregation of the LORD' — the statement comes from the entire assembly.

easy.question: What do they criticize in verse 16?
answers: An ephod
An altar
A synagogue
easy.explanation: They complain about the building of an altar by those people.

easy.question: What is referred to by 'the iniquity of Peor' in verse 17?
answers: The sin of building an altar
A general sin of the people
The sin at Peor — idolatry and immorality
easy.explanation: The text recalls the 'iniquity of Peor', referencing the earlier idolatrous episode at Peor that brought a plague.

medium.question: What did the assembly propose if 'the land of your possession' was ceremonially unclean?
answers: That you move to the LORD's possession where the tabernacle dwells and take possession among us
That they stay and attempt to purify the land locally
That they build an alternative altar nearby
medium.explanation: The assembly suggested crossing over to the LORD's possession where the tabernacle is and taking possession among them rather than rebelling.

medium.question: In the phrase 'What trespass have ye committed against the God of Israel', what does 'trespass' mean?
answers: A neutral action without moral weight
A rebellion or sinful act against the LORD
An act of praise toward God
medium.explanation: Here 'trespass' means rebellion or sin against God — the assembly accuses them of a religious offense.

medium.question: What is said will happen 'tomorrow' if they turn away from the LORD?
answers: The priests will punish them
The people will bless them
The LORD will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel
medium.explanation: Verse 18 warns that if they rebel, the LORD will be angry with the whole congregation — a communal judgment.

challenge.question: How is Achan son of Zerah described in the context of these verses?
answers: As someone who took devoted things and caused wrath on all Israel
As a hero who saved Israel
As a priestly figure performing purification
challenge.explanation: The reference to Achan notes his trespass in the devoted thing brought wrath on the whole congregation — a violation causing national punishment.

challenge.question: Why is the phrase 'beside the altar of the LORD our God' a central point of the accusation?
answers: Because it would allow local festivals without central oversight
Because a separate altar could be seen as rebellion and a rival to the LORD's altar, splitting the worship
Because the new altar was meant for sacrifices to foreign gods
challenge.explanation: The fear is that an altar beside the LORD's would create a parallel cult, undermining the unity of worship and possibly leading to rebellion.

challenge.question: Against whom do the accusations in this chapter fall?
answers: The priests in Jerusalem only
The inhabitants of Shechem only
The tribes beyond the Jordan — Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
challenge.explanation: The context is the tribes who returned to their holdings across the Jordan — Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh — who built the altar.

questions.question: How is Achan son of Zerah described in the context of these verses?
answers: As someone who took devoted things and caused wrath on all Israel
As a hero who saved Israel
As a priestly figure performing purification
questions.explanation: The reference to Achan notes his trespass in the devoted thing brought wrath on the whole congregation — a violation causing national punishment.

questions.question: Why is the phrase 'beside the altar of the LORD our God' a central point of the accusation?
answers: Because it would allow local festivals without central oversight
Because a separate altar could be seen as rebellion and a rival to the LORD's altar, splitting the worship
Because the new altar was meant for sacrifices to foreign gods
questions.explanation: The fear is that an altar beside the LORD's would create a parallel cult, undermining the unity of worship and possibly leading to rebellion.

questions.question: Against whom do the accusations in this chapter fall?
answers: The priests in Jerusalem only
The inhabitants of Shechem only
The tribes beyond the Jordan — Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: The context is the tribes who returned to their holdings across the Jordan — Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh — who built the altar.

paragraphs.title: The Tribes' Defense and the Purpose of the Altar

easy.question: Who spoke to the leaders of the thousands of Israel in verse 21?
answers: The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
Moses and the elders
The tribes of Judah and Simeon
easy.explanation: Verse 21 opens saying the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh spoke to the leaders of the thousands of Israel.

easy.question: What had the Reubenites, Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh built according to the verses?
answers: An altar
A house
A wall
easy.explanation: They state 'we have built us an altar' — they built an altar.

easy.question: Did they intend the altar they built to be used for burnt offerings and sacrifices?
answers: Yes, to offer burnt offerings and sacrifices there
Yes — only for peace offerings
No — they declared 'not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice'
easy.explanation: They explicitly say the altar is not for burnt offerings or sacrifices — its purpose was not for sacrifice.

medium.question: Why did they say they built the altar, according to their explanation?
answers: To start a new separate worship of a different god
To mark a territorial boundary
To serve as a witness between us and you and our generations so descendants won't say they have no part in the LORD
medium.explanation: They explain the altar is a witness between the groups and future generations so no one will claim they have no share in the LORD.

medium.question: In the phrase 'it shall be a witness between us and you', what does 'witness' mean?
answers: A sign/testimony or memorial between the groups
A small altar for sacrifices
A judge who settles disputes
medium.explanation: Here 'witness' refers to a memorial or testimony affirming the shared relationship with the LORD, not a judicial role.

medium.question: What warning do they give in verse 29 when they say 'God forbid that we should rebel against the LORD'?
answers: That building an altar to foreign gods would bring immediate divine punishment
That erecting an altar for sacrifices apart from the LORD's altar would be rebellion and turning from God
That the altar would cause border disputes with neighboring peoples
medium.explanation: They insist they would not rebel by building an altar for sacrifices opposite the LORD's altar — stressing they're faithful, not rebellious.

challenge.question: Why do they emphasize repeatedly that the altar is 'not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice'?
answers: To make clear they did not intend the altar for cultic sacrifice but only as a sign/witness
To show they would use the altar for military purposes
To declare the altar would be the center for new religious expressions
challenge.explanation: The repetition stresses the altar's non-sacrificial function — it was a memorial, not a parallel sacrificial site.

challenge.question: Which tribes/groups are located east of the Jordan in this passage?
answers: Tribes west of the Jordan only
All tribes of Israel including the Levites
The children of Reuben, the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
challenge.explanation: Verse 21 explicitly names Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh as the tribes settled east of the Jordan.

challenge.question: What does the phrase 'beside the altar of the LORD our God that is before his tabernacle' imply about their relation to the central altar?
answers: They intended to replace the altar before the tabernacle with their new altar
Their altar was additional and separate, not meant to replace the LORD's altar
That it forbids any idolatry near the tabernacle
challenge.explanation: The phrase 'beside' indicates the new altar was meant as an additional memorial, not as a replacement for the central altar before the tabernacle.

questions.question: Why do they emphasize repeatedly that the altar is 'not for burnt offering nor for sacrifice'?
answers: To make clear they did not intend the altar for cultic sacrifice but only as a sign/witness
To show they would use the altar for military purposes
To declare the altar would be the center for new religious expressions
questions.explanation: The repetition stresses the altar's non-sacrificial function — it was a memorial, not a parallel sacrificial site.

questions.question: Which tribes/groups are located east of the Jordan in this passage?
answers: Tribes west of the Jordan only
All tribes of Israel including the Levites
The children of Reuben, the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Verse 21 explicitly names Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh as the tribes settled east of the Jordan.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'beside the altar of the LORD our God that is before his tabernacle' imply about their relation to the central altar?
answers: They intended to replace the altar before the tabernacle with their new altar
Their altar was additional and separate, not meant to replace the LORD's altar
That it forbids any idolatry near the tabernacle
questions.explanation: The phrase 'beside' indicates the new altar was meant as an additional memorial, not as a replacement for the central altar before the tabernacle.

easy.question: Who heard the words in the verse?
answers: Phinehas the priest, the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands of Israel
Only Phinehas the priest
Only the Reubenites, Gadites and Manasseh
easy.explanation: The verse specifies that Phinehas, the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands heard the words.

easy.question: Who spoke the words that were heard?
answers: The priests of the tribe of Levi
The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
City leaders
easy.explanation: The verse indicates it was the Reubenites, Gadites and Manasseh who spoke the words.

easy.question: What was the reaction of those who heard the words according to the verse?
answers: They were very angry
They were stunned and did not respond
It pleased them
easy.explanation: The verse ends with 'and it pleased them' — they approved of what was said.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'which were with him' mean in this verse?
answers: The persons who were accompanying him
The documents he carried
The items found on him
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the people who were accompanying Phinehas — those present with him.

medium.question: What does 'it pleased them' mean in the context 'and it pleased them'?
answers: They approved or found it good
They were confused
They cursed and scolded
medium.explanation: 'It pleased them' means they approved and were satisfied with the explanation given.

medium.question: What does the term 'the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands of Israel' indicate in this verse?
answers: That these were solely religious officials
That they were ordinary people without official roles
That they were community leaders at various levels
medium.explanation: The phrase points to leaders of different ranks — religious and civic/military — showing a multi-level leadership structure.

challenge.question: What can be inferred about the leaders' response after hearing the tribes' words?
answers: They immediately imposed a heavy punishment
They ignored the words
They accepted and approved the tribes' explanation
challenge.explanation: The verse states 'and it pleased them', indicating acceptance and approval by the leaders.

challenge.question: Why does the verse list the priest, the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands together?
answers: To show the response included both religious and civil/military leadership
To show only the priest made the decision
To emphasize that only the thousands discussed the matter
challenge.explanation: Listing these groups shows both religious authority and civil/military leadership were involved in the decision.

challenge.question: What does the term 'thousands' imply about society's organization in this period?
answers: That 'thousand' refers to a single large tribe
That there were leadership units or military/civic divisions headed by captains of thousands
That each thousand was made up only of priests
challenge.explanation: 'Thousands' suggests an organizational division led by captains or heads of thousands, indicating social and military structure.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the leaders' response after hearing the tribes' words?
answers: They immediately imposed a heavy punishment
They ignored the words
They accepted and approved the tribes' explanation
questions.explanation: The verse states 'and it pleased them', indicating acceptance and approval by the leaders.

questions.question: Why does the verse list the priest, the leaders of the congregation and the heads of the thousands together?
answers: To show the response included both religious and civil/military leadership
To show only the priest made the decision
To emphasize that only the thousands discussed the matter
questions.explanation: Listing these groups shows both religious authority and civil/military leadership were involved in the decision.

questions.question: What does the term 'thousands' imply about society's organization in this period?
answers: That 'thousand' refers to a single large tribe
That there were leadership units or military/civic divisions headed by captains of thousands
That each thousand was made up only of priests
questions.explanation: 'Thousands' suggests an organizational division led by captains or heads of thousands, indicating social and military structure.

easy.question: Who spoke the words in the verse?
answers: Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest
Joshua
Moses
easy.explanation: The verse begins 'And Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest said' — Phinehas is the speaker.

easy.question: To whom did Phinehas speak in this verse?
answers: To the children of Jacob only
To the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
To the king and his counselors
easy.explanation: Phinehas addressed the Reubenites, Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh directly.

easy.question: What does the statement 'now have ye delivered the children of Israel out of the hand of the LORD' mean?
answers: They brought punishment on Israel
They received a gift from God
They prevented the LORD's punishment or wrath from falling on Israel
easy.explanation: Phinehas says they have averted the LORD's anger from falling on Israel — they saved the people from divine wrath.

medium.question: In the phrase 'that ye have not trespassed against the LORD', what does 'trespassed' mean?
answers: You did acts of charity
You committed treachery or betrayed the LORD
You went on a journey
medium.explanation: Here 'trespassed' means to have violated or rebelled against the LORD — a betrayal of faithfulness.

medium.question: What does Phinehas say is known 'today' regarding the standing of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh?
answers: That the LORD is among them
That they have done evil
That they abandoned the land

paragraphs.title: The Altar as a Witness Between Them

easy.question: Who named the altar in this verse?
answers: The children of Reuben and the children of Gad
Joshua
The high priest
easy.explanation: The verse states 'And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar' — they named it.

easy.question: What name did they give the altar?
answers: A great altar
Ed (a witness)
Place of offerings
easy.explanation: They called the altar 'Ed', meaning a witness between them.

easy.question: Why did they call it that according to the verse?
answers: To offer foreign sacrifices there
To mark territorial boundaries
Because it is a witness between us that the LORD is God
easy.explanation: They named it so because it was to be a witness between them, declaring that the LORD is God.

medium.question: In 'they called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us', what does 'witness' mean?
answers: A sign or testimony/memorial between the groups
An altar used for sacrifices
A judge who settles disputes
medium.explanation: 'Witness' here means a memorial sign attesting the shared relationship with the LORD between the groups.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'for the LORD God' mainly signify in this verse?
answers: A declaration that the LORD is the true God
A comparison between different gods
A random listing of divine names
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes and declares that the LORD is God — a strong religious assertion.

medium.question: What does the word 'between us' imply in the verse?
answers: Between members of the same tribe only
Between the different tribes/groups — a mutual witness
Between a person and God
medium.explanation: 'Between us' indicates the memorial is meant as a testimony between the groups — a sign of their shared faith.

challenge.question: What practical purpose is implied by naming the altar 'Ed' (a witness)?
answers: That it was built for idolatrous worship
That it served as a marker to prevent disputes and accusations between the tribes
That it was intended to be a seat for legal judgments
challenge.explanation: Calling the altar a 'witness' implies it is a memorial to prevent future disputes or claims that one side lacked part in the LORD.

challenge.question: Which word in the clause 'for it shall be a witness' functions to introduce the reason or explanation?
answers: for
witness
it
challenge.explanation: 'For' introduces the explanatory reason: 'for it shall be a witness' explains why they named it so.

challenge.question: Why does the verse use the phrase 'the LORD God' rather than simply 'the LORD' — what is the likely effect?
answers: It indicates worship of foreign gods
The double-form (LORD God) strengthens and emphasizes the declaration that the LORD is the true God
It's meaningless — just a random wording
challenge.explanation: Using both titles serves to strengthen and emphasize the claim that the LORD is their God — a forceful theological affirmation.
